Name: Cancer
Short description:
RoMIUS Urology provides expert, compassionate care for women diagnosed with urologic cancers. Although kidney and bladder cancers are less common in women than men, they often present differently and may be diagnosed later. Our team prioritizes timely evaluation, advanced diagnostics, and multidisciplinary treatment planning to ensure women receive the highest level of care throughout Northwest and West Central Ohio.
We partner closely with medical oncology, radiation oncology, imaging specialists, and primary care providers to deliver seamless, comprehensive cancer care from diagnosis through survivorship.
Long description:
Kidney Cancer in Women

Kidney cancer can affect women of all ages and often presents with symptoms such as flank pain, blood in the urine, or incidental findings on imaging.

RoMIUS Urology offers:

Advanced Diagnostic Evaluation

  • High-resolution CT or MRI
  • Urinalysis and laboratory testing
  • Ultrasound for surveillance or follow-up

State-of-the-Art Treatment Options

Our surgeons are regional leaders in:

  • Robotic partial nephrectomy (nephron-sparing surgery)
  • Robotic radical nephrectomy for advanced disease
  • Ablative therapies for select small lesions
  • Active surveillance for low-risk tumors

We emphasize kidney preservation whenever safely possible, particularly important for women with long life expectancy or underlying health concerns.

Multidisciplinary Collaboration

For advanced or metastatic kidney cancer, we work closely with medical oncology to coordinate immunotherapy and targeted systemic treatments, ensuring each patient receives an individualized and effective care plan.

Bladder Cancer in Women

Bladder cancer in women can sometimes be misdiagnosed initially as recurrent UTIs or bladder irritation, delaying detection. RoMIUS Urology focuses on early identification and timely management to optimize outcomes.

Comprehensive Evaluation & Testing

  • In-office cystoscopy
  • Urinalysis and culture
  • Urine cytology for cancer detection
  • CT urogram or ultrasound imaging

Cutting-Edge Intravesical Therapy

We offer the most advanced intravesical treatments, including:

  • Immunotherapy (e.g., BCG)
  • Chemotherapy instillations
  • Risk-based maintenance protocols

These therapies are tailored to the tumor grade, stage, and recurrence pattern.

Advanced Surgical Expertise

For more complex or muscle-invasive disease, our team performs:

  • Robotic radical cystectomy
  • Urinary reconstruction options tailored to each patient
  • Coordination with medical and radiation oncology

Women receive a highly personalized plan addressing cancer control, quality of life, urinary function, and long-term surveillance.

Why Women Trust RoMIUS Urology

  • Expertise in female urologic cancers
  • Fast evaluation of symptoms like hematuria or recurrent UTIs
  • Access to cutting-edge minimally invasive and robotic surgery
  • Advanced intravesical therapies for bladder cancer
  • Collaborative care with oncology and imaging specialists
  • Clear communication and compassionate support
  • Long-term surveillance to ensure early detection of recurrence

Name: Urinary Problems
Short description:
RoMIUS Urology provides specialized, compassionate care for women experiencing urinary symptoms that affect quality of life, daily activities, and sleep. Whether symptoms come from bladder dysfunction, pelvic floor issues, incontinence, or the need for catheter management, our team delivers individualized, evidence-based treatment using the latest technologies and diagnostic tools.
We proudly serve women across Northwest and West Central Ohio with attentive, patient-centered care.
Long description:
Incontinence

Urinary incontinence is extremely common in women and may result from childbirth, pelvic floor weakness, hormonal changes, aging, or prior surgeries. We carefully differentiate between:

Types of Incontinence

  • Stress Incontinence – leakage with coughing, laughing, activity
  • Urge Incontinence – sudden urge followed by leakage
  • Mixed Incontinence – combination of stress + urge

Treatment Options

  • Pelvic floor physical therapy
  • Behavioral and bladder training
  • Medications for urgency leakage
  • Urethral bulking agents
  • Pessary fitting
  • Mid-urethral sling surgery
  • Neuromodulation for refractory urgency

Every care plan is personalized to each woman’s anatomy and goals.

Overactive Bladder (OAB)

Overactive bladder causes urinary urgency, frequency, and strong uncontrollable urges—sometimes with incontinence. It can significantly impact confidence, daily activity, and sleep.

Our Tiered OAB Treatment Approach

  • Lifestyle modifications and fluid timing
  • Pelvic floor physical therapy
  • Bladder medications
  • Botox® bladder injections

Neuromodulation Expertise

For women with persistent, refractory symptoms, we offer Sacral Neuromodulation (InterStim®).
RoMIUS Urology is recognized as a Medtronic Center of Excellence for InterStim therapy, reflecting our high level of experience, surgical volume, and exceptional outcomes with neuromodulation.

This advanced therapy offers long-term bladder control for women whose symptoms have not responded to traditional treatments.

Nighttime Urination (Nocturia)

Nocturia disrupts sleep and overall well-being. Common causes include bladder irritation, overactive bladder, hormonal changes, fluid imbalance, and sleep apnea.

Evaluation includes bladder scans, urine testing, lifestyle assessment, and optional sleep or hormonal evaluation.
Treatment blends behavioral strategies, pelvic therapy, medications, and bladder-targeted interventions to reduce nighttime awakenings and restore restorative sleep.

Chronic Catheter Management

Some women require catheter support due to retention, neurologic conditions, bladder dysfunction, or surgical recovery.

RoMIUS Urology provides comprehensive catheter care, including:

  • Foley catheter management
  • Suprapubic catheter care and placement
  • Intermittent self-catheterization training
  • Regular catheter changes
  • Skin and infection prevention guidance
  • Evaluation for catheter-free alternatives

We focus on maximizing comfort, minimizing infections, and restoring independence.

Incontinence Management (Advanced Options)

For women with more severe or persistent leakage, we provide the full range of modern, minimally invasive interventions:

  • Pelvic floor therapy
  • Medications for urgency
  • Neuromodulation (InterStim®)
  • Mid-urethral sling surgery
  • Urethral bulking procedures

Our objective is to restore confidence, comfort, and long-term bladder control.

Why Women Trust RoMIUS Urology

  • Specialized expertise in female urinary disorders
  • Gentle, thorough evaluation
  • Strong integration with pelvic floor therapy
  • Minimally invasive surgical options
  • Recognized Center of Excellence for Medtronic InterStim neuromodulation
  • Personalized, supportive care
  • Long-term follow-up and symptom monitoring

Name: Kidney Stones
Short description: Kidney stones can cause sudden, severe pain and require timely evaluation and intervention. RoMIUS Urology provides rapid access to care across multiple emergency departments and uses an advanced triage system to ensure patients are evaluated quickly, treated appropriately, and supported throughout every stage of their stone episode. Whether working through a trial of passage or needing urgent surgical intervention, our team offers expert, personalized, and compassionate care.
Long description:
‍Timely Evaluation & Rapid Access

Kidney stone pain is unpredictable, and delays in care can lead to complications. RoMIUS Urology maintains direct coverage at multiple emergency departments across Northwest and West Central Ohio, ensuring rapid diagnosis and smoother transitions to definitive treatment.

Our advanced triage system prioritizes patients based on symptoms, infection risk, imaging findings, and obstruction severity—allowing us to expedite evaluation, coordinate immediate surgery when needed, and prevent ER delays.

Tailored Treatment Plans

Every kidney stone is different, and so is every patient. We guide individuals through the decision-making process, helping them choose between:

  • Trial of passage
  • Ureteroscopy
  • Extracorporeal Shock Wave Lithotripsy (ESWL)
  • Percutaneous Nephrolithotomy (PCNL) for large or complex stones

We support patients attempting to pass their stone safely at home and provide immediate access to intervention if pain becomes uncontrolled, infection develops, or the trial of passage becomes unsafe or unsuccessful. Our goal is to balance safety, speed, comfort, and patient preference.

Stent Management & Symptom Support

Following stone surgery, some patients require a temporary ureteral stent to ensure safe drainage of the kidney. Stents can cause discomfort, urinary urgency, frequency, or flank pain.

RoMIUS Urology provides comprehensive stent management, including:

  • Medications to control bladder spasms and stent discomfort
  • Pain control strategies tailored to each patient
  • Guidance on activity, hydration, and symptom triggers
  • Rapid access for questions and concerns
  • Timely scheduling for stent removal or exchange

Our team ensures patients feel supported throughout the recovery process, minimizing discomfort and helping them return to normal activity quickly and safely.

Advanced Surgical Expertise

RoMIUS Urology is home to the most experienced stone surgeons in the region, performing high volumes of ureteroscopy, ESWL, and PCNL with excellent outcomes.
Using high-powered lasers, modern digital endoscopes, and advanced imaging, we manage everything from small ureteral stones to large staghorn calculi with precision and efficiency.

Our experience translates directly into safer procedures, faster recovery, and better long-term results for our patients.

Prevention & Long-Term Management

Because kidney stones often recur, RoMIUS Urology focuses heavily on prevention. We provide:

  • Comprehensive metabolic evaluation
  • 24-hour urine analysis
  • Stone composition analysis
  • Dietary and hydration counseling
  • Medication therapy when indicated
  • Long-term surveillance and imaging protocols

Our goal is to reduce recurrence risk and help patients avoid repeated ER visits, procedures, or long-term kidney complications.

Why Patients Trust RoMIUS Urology for Kidney Stone Care

  • Rapid access and coordinated care across multiple EDs
  • Immediate surgical availability when needed
  • Tailored treatment pathways with ongoing support
  • Regional leaders in ureteroscopy, ESWL, and PCNL
  • Comprehensive stent, pain, and symptom management
  • Complete metabolic evaluation and long-term prevention
  • A patient-centered approach focused on comfort and durable outcomes

Name: Other Urologic Problems
Short description:
Not every urologic concern fits neatly into a single category. From pelvic organ prolapse to voiding dysfunction, urethral conditions, and other less common issues, RoMIUS Urology provides expert evaluation and treatment for the full range of women's urologic health concerns.
Whatever you're experiencing, we're here to help you find answers.
Long description:
What Falls Under "Other Urologic Problems"?

Urologic health is broad, and many women experience symptoms that don't fit into a single, well-defined category. This can include:

  • Pelvic organ prolapse (bladder, uterine, or vaginal)
  • Voiding dysfunction (difficulty starting, weak stream, incomplete emptying)
  • Urethral diverticulum
  • Urethral stricture
  • Overactive bladder (OAB)
  • Stress urinary incontinence
  • Neurogenic bladder
  • Congenital or structural urologic abnormalities
  • Post-surgical or post-radiation urologic complications
  • Fistulas (bladder, urethral, or vaginal)
  • Sexual dysfunction with a urologic component

Because these conditions vary widely in cause and presentation, an individualized evaluation is the first step toward the right treatment.

Our Approach to Evaluation

RoMIUS Urology takes a thorough, patient-centered approach to identifying the source of your symptoms:

  • Detailed history and physical examination
  • Urinalysis and urine culture
  • Bladder diary and symptom tracking
  • Urodynamic testing when indicated
  • Cystoscopy when indicated
  • Imaging (ultrasound, CT, or MRI) as needed
  • Pelvic floor assessment
  • Review of prior surgeries, deliveries, or pelvic trauma

This comprehensive workup allows us to pinpoint the underlying issue, even when symptoms are unusual or difficult to categorize.

Pelvic Organ Prolapse

Prolapse occurs when pelvic organs — the bladder, uterus, or rectum — shift from their normal position due to weakened pelvic support. Symptoms can include:

  • A sensation of pelvic pressure or bulging
  • Difficulty emptying the bladder
  • Urinary leakage
  • Discomfort during activity or intercourse

Treatment options range from pelvic floor physical therapy and pessary fitting to surgical repair, depending on severity and patient goals.

Voiding Dysfunction and Overactive Bladder

Difficulty with normal bladder emptying, or the opposite — urgency and frequency without infection — can significantly affect daily life. We offer:

  • Behavioral and dietary modification
  • Pelvic floor physical therapy
  • Medications for bladder relaxation or emptying
  • Botox® for refractory overactive bladder
  • Sacral neuromodulation (InterStim®) for severe cases
  • Clean intermittent catheterization training when needed

Structural and Post-Surgical Concerns

Some women develop urologic issues following childbirth, prior pelvic surgery, or radiation treatment — including strictures, fistulas, or scar-related complications. We coordinate closely with gynecology, colorectal, and pelvic floor specialists to manage these complex cases with a team-based approach.

Why Women Choose RoMIUS Urology

  • Expertise across the full spectrum of women's urologic conditions
  • Willingness to investigate symptoms that don't fit a standard diagnosis
  • Advanced diagnostic tools, including urodynamics
  • Strong collaboration with pelvic floor therapists and other specialists
  • Compassionate, unhurried evaluations
  • Personalized treatment plans, from conservative to surgical options

Name: Sexual Health
Short description: RoMIUS Urology provides advanced, compassionate care for men experiencing sexual health concerns. Our specialists offer state-of-the-art diagnostics, medical therapies, and minimally invasive treatments—tailored to restore confidence, improve function, and enhance overall quality of life. We treat the full spectrum of male sexual health conditions with expertise, discretion, and a patient-centered approach for men throughout Northwest and West Central Ohio.
Long description:
Erectile Dysfunction (ED)

Erectile dysfunction is one of the most common men’s health concerns, and RoMIUS Urology provides the full range of modern, evidence-based treatments. Our evaluation identifies root causes such as vascular disease, hormonal imbalance, nerve injury, or medication effects so patients receive truly personalized care.

A key part of our philosophy is guiding patients toward the most cost-effective treatment options, especially since many ED therapies are elective and not always covered by insurance. We help patients navigate affordable medication pathways, generics, compounding options, and cost-efficient device therapies to ensure they receive high-value care without unnecessary expense.

RoMIUS Urology is also recognized as a center of excellence for penile implantation, having performed the highest volume of penile implants in the region with exceptional outcomes and patient satisfaction. For patients who require long-term correction, our expertise in prosthetic urology offers safe, effective, and durable solutions.

Peyronie’s Disease

Peyronie’s disease may cause penile curvature, pain, or difficulty with sexual function. RoMIUS Urology offers the latest diagnostic tools and a complete spectrum of treatments—from medical management and collagenase (Xiaflex®) injections to minimally invasive or surgical straightening procedures when necessary. Our goal is to restore both form and function, helping patients regain confidence with individualized, outcome-driven care.

Testosterone Therapy

Low testosterone (hypogonadism) can affect energy, libido, mood, muscle mass, and overall well-being. We provide a thorough, evidence-based evaluation to distinguish true hormone deficiency from other causes of symptoms. Treatment options include topical gels, short- and long-acting injections, and long-duration pellet implants. Each patient receives a customized monitoring plan to ensure safe, effective, and optimized hormone therapy. We also account for fertility preservation, metabolic health, and long-term hormonal balance.

Premature Ejaculation (PE)

Premature ejaculation is one of the most common and under-treated men’s sexual health concerns. RoMIUS Urology offers evidence-based treatments including topical anesthetics, oral medications, pelvic floor therapies, and behavioral strategies. We focus on improving control, reducing anxiety, and restoring confidence for both patients and couples through personalized, effective management.

Low Libido / Sexual Desire Concerns

Decreased sexual desire can stem from hormonal imbalance, stress, chronic illness, fatigue, medication effects, or relationship factors. Our team performs a comprehensive evaluation—including hormone testing, metabolic screening, and psychological contributors—to identify the true cause. Treatments are tailored to restore healthy sexual desire, improve overall well-being, and support long-term sexual health.

Name: Urinary Problems
Short description: RoMIUS Urology provides comprehensive evaluation and treatment for the full range of urinary symptoms affecting men. Whether related to prostate enlargement, bladder dysfunction, infections, retention, strictures, or incontinence, our team uses advanced diagnostics and individualized therapies to improve urinary function, comfort, and overall quality of life. We offer both office-based and minimally invasive treatment options tailored to each patient’s needs across Northwest and West Central Ohio.
Long description:
Enlarged Prostate (BPH)

Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), or enlarged prostate, is one of the most common causes of urinary symptoms in men. With so many treatment options available, the decision can feel overwhelming—we take pride in guiding patients toward the most effective, durable treatments with the best outcomes for their specific circumstances.

RoMIUS Urology provides a full spectrum of BPH therapies, ranging from lifestyle adjustments and medical therapy to advanced minimally invasive and surgical interventions. Our specialists perform state-of-the-art procedures including:

  • UroLift®
  • GreenLight™ Photovaporization of the Prostate — RoMIUS Urology is a regional Center of Excellence, performing high volumes with outstanding safety and outcomes.
  • Transurethral Resection of the Prostate (TURP)
  • Prostate Artery Embolization (PAE)
  • Robotic Simple Prostatectomy for very large glands or severe obstruction

Each treatment plan is personalized to improve urinary flow, reduce nighttime urination, and enhance bladder emptying—all with an emphasis on long-term success, comfort, and helping patients confidently choose the therapy that best fits their goals and anatomy.

Overactive Bladder (OAB)

Overactive bladder causes urinary urgency, frequency, and sudden uncontrollable urges. RoMIUS Urology takes a structured, evidence-based approach to diagnosis and treatment, tailored to each patient’s symptom pattern and bladder function.

Therapies include:

  • Pelvic floor physical therapy
  • Lifestyle and behavioral strategies
  • Bladder medications
  • Sacral neuromodulation (InterStim®) — RoMIUS Urology is a Medtronic Center of Excellence for InterStim therapy and is recognized as the highest-volume provider of sacral neuromodulation in the region.
  • Bladder Botox® injections
  • Other minimally invasive nerve therapies

Our goal is to restore bladder control and improve long-term reliability, comfort, and quality of life.

Nighttime Urination (Nocturia)

Nighttime urination can significantly disrupt sleep and overall wellbeing. Causes may include prostate obstruction, bladder irritation, fluid imbalance, hormonal changes, or sleep disorders like sleep apnea. We evaluate each contributing factor and tailor treatment with lifestyle modifications, medications, bladder-directed therapies, and prostate interventions to reduce nighttime awakenings and support more restorative sleep.

Bladder Infections (UTIs)

Men with bladder infections require careful evaluation to uncover underlying causes such as urinary retention, prostate enlargement, kidney stones, or bladder dysfunction.
RoMIUS Urology provides streamlined diagnostics, targeted antibiotic therapies, and prevention strategies to reduce recurrence. For patients with recurrent or complicated infections, we perform deeper assessments of bladder emptying, urinary flow, and prostate anatomy to ensure long-term resolution and urinary health.

Chronic Catheter Management

Many men require long-term catheter support due to urinary retention, neurologic conditions, prostate obstruction, or bladder dysfunction. RoMIUS Urology specializes in chronic catheter management, offering individualized care plans that prioritize comfort, safety, and infection prevention.

We provide comprehensive management of:

  • Long-term Foley catheters
  • Suprapubic catheters
  • Intermittent self-catheterization programs
  • Catheter change schedules, skin care, and infection mitigation
  • Evaluation for catheter-free alternatives such as BPH therapies, bladder procedures, or neuromodulation

Our team focuses on minimizing complications and exploring solutions that may allow patients to return to more natural bladder function whenever possible.

Incontinence Management

Urinary leakage in men often results from prostate surgery, radiation, sphincter weakness, or neurologic conditions. RoMIUS Urology offers the full range of modern treatments, from conservative therapies to advanced surgical correction.

We are recognized as a regional leader and for Artificial Urinary Sphincter (AUS) and Advance Male Sling—the gold-standard surgical treatments for male stress urinary incontinence. Our surgeons are among the most experienced at implantation in the region, with extensive expertise in primary implantation and revision surgery.

Treatment options include:

  • Pelvic floor therapy
  • Lifestyle modifications
  • Medications for urgency
  • Male slings
  • Artificial Urinary Sphincter (AUS) 

Our goal is to restore continence, confidence, and quality of life through individualized, evidence-based care.

Urethral Strictures

Urethral strictures—narrowing of the urinary channel—can cause weak stream, urinary retention, infections, painful urination, or the inability to empty the bladder completely.

RoMIUS Urology is one of the only regional practices with providers who have advanced, specialized training in urethral reconstruction and complex stricture management. This expertise allows us to diagnose strictures accurately and offer a full suite of treatments, including:

  • Endoscopic dilation
  • Direct visual internal urethrotomy (DVIU)
  • Urethral reconstruction
  • Substitution urethroplasty
  • Stricture surveillance and long-term management

Our goal is to restore normal urinary flow and prevent recurrence through expert, highly individualized care.

Name: Family Planning and Vasectomy
Short description: RoMIUS Urology offers comprehensive, patient-centered care for men seeking permanent contraception through vasectomy. As leaders in men’s reproductive health, our team provides expert counseling, advanced techniques, and comfortable treatment options—ensuring a smooth experience from consultation through recovery.
Long description:
What Is a Vasectomy?

A vasectomy is a safe, effective, and permanent form of male contraception. The procedure works by blocking the vas deferens—the tubes that carry sperm from the testicles—so sperm is no longer present in the semen.
It does not affect testosterone levels, sexual function, erections, libido, or overall masculinity.

Vasectomy is one of the most reliable birth control methods and is a popular choice for men and couples who have completed their family or want long-term contraception without ongoing maintenance.

Sedation or Local Anesthesia Options

RoMIUS Urology offers vasectomy in the way that best matches each patient’s comfort level:

  • Local Anesthesia (In-Office):
    A quick and highly tolerable option performed entirely in the office. Patients remain awake and comfortable during a short procedure with minimal downtime.
  • Sedation (Ambulatory Setting):
    For patients who prefer a more relaxed experience, we offer vasectomy under light sedation in an outpatient surgical environment. This is ideal for men with anxiety, prior negative experiences, or just a preference for maximal comfort.

Because we offer both approaches, patients can choose the setting and anesthetic method that suits them best.

No-Scalpel & Traditional Vasectomy Techniques

RoMIUS Urology performs both no-scalpel and traditional vasectomy techniques, allowing us to tailor the procedure to each patient’s anatomy and preferences:

No-Scalpel Vasectomy

  • Uses a tiny puncture instead of incisions
  • Minimal bleeding and very low complication rates
  • Faster recovery and less postoperative discomfort
  • Popular for men wanting the least invasive approach

Traditional Vasectomy

  • Involves two small incisions
  • Allows direct visualization of the vas deferens
  • Ideal for certain anatomical variations or prior surgeries
  • Offers the same long-term effectiveness

Both methods are highly effective, and your surgeon will help determine which technique is best for your specific anatomy and goals.

Quick Recovery & Aftercare

Most men return to normal activities within a couple of days, with full recovery in about one week.
We provide clear instructions on:

  • Activity restrictions
  • Ice and pain control
  • When to resume sexual activity
  • How to avoid complications
  • Scheduling post-vasectomy semen testing

Our team remains available for questions and support throughout the recovery process.

Semen Analysis & Confirmation of Sterility

A vasectomy is not immediately effective. We perform follow-up semen analysis to confirm sterility before patients discontinue other forms of birth control.
This step is essential—and we make the process easy, discreet, and efficient.

Why Choose RoMIUS Urology for Vasectomy?

  • Multiple anesthesia options, including local or sedation
  • Expertise in no-scalpel and traditional vasectomy
  • Fast, convenient scheduling and minimal downtime
  • Detailed counseling and personalized care
  • Comfortable, patient-centered approach
  • Experienced urologists with thousands of procedures performed

Name: Cancer
Short description: RoMIUS Urology provides comprehensive, state-of-the-art care for the full spectrum of urologic cancers. Our team combines advanced diagnostics, robotic and minimally invasive surgery, multidisciplinary collaboration, and personalized treatment planning to deliver exceptional outcomes for patients across Northwest and West Central Ohio.
Long description:
Prostate Cancer

RoMIUS Urology offers complete, coordinated care for men with prostate cancer—from early detection to advanced treatment pathways. We are the regional leaders in robotic prostatectomy, having performed the highest volume of minimally invasive prostate cancer surgery in the Northwest and West Central Ohio region with exceptional outcomes.

As part of our advanced prostate cancer program, we have integrated URO Pharmacy, a specialty pharmacy with a dedicated urology-specific pharmacist and pharmacy technician. This team works directly with our providers to optimize systemic therapy selections, streamline access to medications, and support patients throughout their treatment journey.

We collaborate closely with radiation oncology and medical oncology partners across the region to ensure each patient receives a fully coordinated, multidisciplinary plan—whether that includes active surveillance, radiation therapy, hormonal therapy, systemic treatments, or surgery.

Kidney Cancer

Our surgeons are leaders in robotic and minimally invasive kidney surgery, specializing in partial (nephron-sparing) nephrectomy, complex tumor removal, and techniques designed to preserve kidney function whenever possible. We offer comprehensive evaluation for kidney masses, including advanced imaging, biopsy when appropriate, and personalized surveillance protocols for small renal lesions.

For patients with advanced or metastatic renal cell carcinoma, we collaborate closely with medical oncology to coordinate systemic therapies such as immunotherapy and targeted agents. This multidisciplinary partnership ensures each patient receives the most modern, effective, and individualized treatment plan across all stages of kidney cancer.

Bladder Cancer

RoMIUS Urology provides expert care across the full spectrum of bladder cancer, with a focus on early detection, in-office cystoscopy, and the most cutting-edge intravesical treatments—including advanced immunotherapy and chemotherapy instillation protocols tailored to tumor grade, stage, and recurrence risk.

For patients with more advanced disease, our team performs robotic radical cystectomy and complex urinary reconstruction with precision and a focus on functional outcomes. We work closely with oncology colleagues to deliver coordinated, stage-appropriate treatment from diagnosis through long-term surveillance and survivorship.

Testicular Cancer

We emphasize rapid evaluation and early diagnosis for testicular cancer, with attention to fertility preservation and minimally invasive treatment. Our surgeons emphasize prompt evaluation with subsequent radical orchiectomy and coordinate chemotherapy, surveillance, and long-term follow-up planning with regional oncology teams. This collaborative, streamlined approach helps achieve high cure rates and individualized care for every patient.

Name: Pelvic and Testicular Pain
Short description: Chronic pelvic or testicular pain can be frustrating, disruptive, and difficult to diagnose. RoMIUS Urology provides a systematic, multidisciplinary approach to evaluate and treat men suffering from pelvic pain, chronic testicular discomfort, prostate-related pain, or interstitial cystitis–like symptoms. Our goal is to identify the true source of pain and create a personalized plan that restores comfort, function, and quality of life.
Long description:
Comprehensive Evaluation of Pelvic Pain

Men’s pelvic pain can arise from many causes, including:

  • Pelvic floor dysfunction
  • Neuromuscular issues
  • Chronic prostatitis (infectious or inflammatory)
  • Interstitial cystitis–like bladder pain
  • Urethral pathology or strictures
  • Referred pain from the back, spine, or hips
  • Nerve entrapment
  • Epididymal or testicular disorders

Our diagnostic process includes physical examination, imaging, targeted testing, evaluation of pelvic floor dysfunction, and review of spine/hip mechanics to determine the true source of symptoms.

Pelvic Floor Dysfunction & Physical Therapy

Many men with pelvic or testicular pain actually have pelvic floor muscle dysfunction rather than a urologic infection.
We partner with specialized pelvic floor physical therapists who address:

  • Pelvic muscle tension or spasm
  • Trigger points
  • Core and posture mechanics
  • Low-back or hip dysfunction
  • Neuromuscular contributions

This approach often leads to significant improvement.

Chronic Testicular Pain (Orchialgia)

Chronic testicular pain can stem from nerve irritation, pelvic floor dysfunction, epididymal issues, or referred pain from the spine.

Conservative therapies:

  • Anti-inflammatory medications
  • Neuropathic pain medications
  • Pelvic floor therapy
  • Supportive care

Advanced procedural options:

  • Spermatic cord blocks
  • Microsurgical spermatic cord denervation (high success rates)
  • Treatment of varicoceles or epididymal pathology when appropriate
  • Addressing referred pain from the spine or hips

We offer a structured, stepwise management plan tailored to each patient.

Prostate Pain & Prostatitis

Prostatitis may be:

  • Bacterial
  • Inflammatory (non-infectious)
  • Pelvic floor–related
  • Neuropathic
  • Referred from bladder or urethra

We treat prostatitis with evidence-based methods:

  • Targeted antibiotics only when appropriate
  • Anti-inflammatory medications
  • Pelvic floor therapy
  • Alpha-blockers
  • Lifestyle modifications
  • Management of inflammatory chronic pelvic pain syndrome

We also rule out stones, strictures, or bladder issues that mimic prostatitis.

Urethral Pathology Evaluation

Persistent pelvic or testicular pain may result from:

  • Urethral strictures
  • Bladder neck obstruction
  • Irritative bladder conditions

We evaluate with cystoscopy, flow testing, and imaging to ensure structural causes are not missed.

Benign Scrotal Conditions: Hydroceles, Spermatoceles & Testicular Lesions

Name: Recurrent UTI and Perimenopause
Short description: RoMIUS Urology provides specialized care for women experiencing recurrent urinary tract infections (UTIs) as well as the bladder and vaginal changes associated with perimenopause. Although these conditions can overlap in some patients, many women experience them independently. Our goal is to evaluate each concern thoroughly and develop a treatment plan tailored to your specific symptoms and needs.
Long description:
Recurrent Urinary Tract Infections (UTIs)

Recurrent UTIs are common and can significantly disrupt daily life. They are defined as:

  • Two infections within six months, or
  • Three infections within one year

At RoMIUS Urology, we focus on identifying the true cause of repeated infections and providing long-term prevention strategies.

Causes of Recurrent UTIs

Recurrent infections may be related to:

  • Bladder emptying issues
  • Sexual activity
  • Pelvic floor dysfunction
  • Vaginal flora imbalance
  • Bladder stones or anatomical concerns
  • Post-menopausal changes
  • Incomplete treatment of prior infections

Each case requires careful evaluation to determine the underlying cause.

Evaluation

Your assessment may include:

  • Urinalysis and culture
  • Bladder scan to assess emptying
  • Cystoscopy when indicated
  • Ultrasound or CT imaging (if needed)
  • Pelvic examination
  • Review of contributing factors such as hydration, bowel habits, and sexual health

We focus on accurate diagnosis to avoid unnecessary antibiotic use.

Treatment & Prevention

Treatment is individualized based on your specific situation and may include:

  • Culture-directed antibiotics
  • Short-term preventive antibiotic strategies (when appropriate)
  • Hydration and lifestyle adjustments
  • Pelvic floor physical therapy
  • Supplements such as D-mannose or probiotics
  • Addressing bladder emptying or anatomical issues
  • Vaginal estrogen therapy for post-menopausal patients (when indicated)

Our goal is to break the cycle of repeated infections and improve long-term bladder health.

Perimenopause Symptoms

Perimenopause brings hormonal changes that can affect the urinary tract, vaginal tissue, pelvic floor, and overall comfort. These symptoms may occur with or without recurrent UTIs.

Common Symptoms

Women may experience:

  • Vaginal dryness or irritation
  • Painful intercourse
  • Burning or sensitivity
  • Bladder urgency or frequency
  • Nighttime urination
  • Mild bladder irritation
  • Pelvic pressure
  • Increased susceptibility to discomfort during urination

These symptoms are due to estrogen loss and changes in tissue elasticity, lubrication, and support.

Evaluation

Our evaluation is gentle and thorough and may include:

  • Pelvic examination
  • Discussion of sexual and hormonal history
  • Assessment for vaginal atrophy
  • Bladder function evaluation
  • Review of urinary symptoms
  • Consideration of pelvic floor dysfunction

This helps us determine the right treatment path for your needs.

Treatment Options

We offer a variety of therapies, including:

Hormonal Options

  • Vaginal estrogen (cream, tablet, or ring)
  • Low-dose, non-systemic therapy

These options help restore vaginal and urethral tissue health.

Non-Hormonal Options

  • Vaginal moisturizers and lubricants
  • Hyaluronic acid products
  • Pelvic floor physical therapy
  • Supplements
  • Lifestyle modification

Bladder-Directed Treatments

For women with bladder-specific symptoms, treatment may include:

  • Overactive bladder medications
  • Bladder Botox
  • Neuromodulation
  • Bladder instillations

Why Women Choose RoMIUS Urology

  • Accurate, evidence-based evaluation
  • Personalized treatment plans
  • Options ranging from conservative care to minimally invasive treatments
  • Focus on long-term comfort, confidence, and bladder health
  • Collaborative care with pelvic floor therapy and gynecology when needed

Name: Pelvic Organ Prolapse
Short description:
Expert Treatment Including Anterior Repair & Robotic Sacrocolpopexy
Pelvic organ prolapse (POP) occurs when pelvic floor support weakens, allowing the bladder, uterus, vagina, or rectum to descend. These changes can cause pressure, urinary problems, difficulty with bowel movements, or a visible bulge. POP is common and highly treatable — and RoMIUS Urology provides advanced, compassionate care for all forms of prolapse.
We specialize in minimally invasive pelvic floor reconstruction, offering a full spectrum of treatments from pelvic floor therapy to advanced robotic surgery.
Long description:
Types of Pelvic Organ Prolapse We Treat

Anterior Prolapse (Cystocele)

The bladder drops into the vaginal canal, often causing:

  • Pressure or heaviness
  • Urinary leakage or urgency
  • Difficulty emptying the bladder
  • Recurrent UTIs
  • A bulge at the vaginal opening

Apical Prolapse (Uterine or Vaginal Vault)

The uterus or top of the vagina descends due to loss of pelvic support.

Posterior Prolapse (Rectocele)

The rectum bulges forward into the vagina, causing:

  • Incomplete bowel emptying
  • Constipation
  • Vaginal pressure

Urethral Hypermobility

Loss of support under the urethra can cause stress urinary incontinence.

Symptoms of Pelvic Organ Prolapse

  • Pelvic pressure or heaviness
  • Sensation of a vaginal bulge
  • Urinary urgency, leakage, or retention
  • Difficulty emptying the bladder
  • Constipation or straining
  • Pain during intimacy
  • Recurrent UTIs
  • Tampon “falling out” sensation

Evaluation

RoMIUS Urology performs a comprehensive, gentle assessment that includes:

  • Pelvic exam
  • Grading of prolapse severity
  • Pelvic floor strength testing
  • Bladder emptying evaluation
  • Imaging when needed
  • Hormonal evaluation (post-menopausal changes)
  • Review of childbirth history & prior surgeries

This helps us build a personalized treatment plan tailored to anatomy, symptoms, and goals.

Treatment Options

1. Conservative Treatments

For mild to moderate prolapse or women preferring non-surgical care:

  • Pelvic floor physical therapy
  • Vaginal estrogen
  • Activity and lifestyle adjustments
  • Pessary fitting and management
  • Treatment of coexisting bladder symptoms

2. Surgical Treatment Options

RoMIUS Urology offers advanced, durable surgical solutions including:

Anterior Repair (Cystocele Repair)

Rebuilds support under the bladder to eliminate pressure, bulging, and urinary symptoms.
Performed:

  • Minimally invasively
  • With strong, natural tissue support
  • As outpatient surgery in most cases

Robotic Sacrocolpopexy (Gold Standard for Apical Prolapse)

This is the most durable, anatomic repair for apical prolapse. Using tiny incisions and robotic precision, the vagina (or uterus with hysteropexy) is restored to normal position using a supportive graft.

Benefits of Sacrocolpopexy

  • Long-term anatomic success
  • Excellent support for anterior & apical defects
  • Faster recovery
  • Minimal pain
  • High durability compared to vaginal repairs

Rectocele Repair

Restores posterior vaginal support and improves bowel function.

Urethral Support Procedures

For leakage caused by urethral hypermobility, we offer:

  • Mid-urethral sling
  • Urethral bulking
  • Pelvic floor therapy

Why Women Choose RoMIUS Urology for Pelvic Organ Prolapse

  • Expertise in anterior repairs and pelvic reconstruction
  • Advanced robotic sacrocolpopexy capabilities
  • Conservative + surgical options tailored to each woman
  • Strong integration with pelvic floor therapy
  • Evidence-based, minimally invasive approach
  • Focus on restoring confidence, comfort, and function
  • Comprehensive follow-up and long-term support

Name: Pelvic Pain and Interstitial Cystitis
Short description:
Chronic pelvic pain and bladder pain/interstitial cystitis (IC) can be debilitating, frustrating, and often misunderstood. Many women suffer for years without a clear diagnosis. RoMIUS Urology provides a structured, compassionate, multidisciplinary approach to identify the true source of pain and deliver targeted, effective treatment.
We take pelvic pain seriously — and we specialize in finding answers.
Long description:
What Is Pelvic Pain?

Pelvic pain in women can stem from many different causes, including:

  • Pelvic floor muscle dysfunction
  • Bladder pain syndrome / Interstitial cystitis (IC)
  • Recurrent bladder irritation
  • Endometriosis
  • Pudendal nerve irritation
  • Urethral irritation
  • Pelvic organ prolapse
  • Postpartum pelvic trauma
  • Hormonal changes
  • Spine, hip, or musculoskeletal issues
  • Prior surgeries or scar tissue

Because pelvic pain may originate from multiple sources, an accurate diagnosis is essential.

What Is Interstitial Cystitis (IC)?

Interstitial cystitis (IC), also known as bladder pain syndrome, is a chronic condition characterized by:

  • Bladder or pelvic pain
  • Urinary urgency
  • Urinary frequency
  • Pressure or burning
  • Symptoms worsening with bladder filling
  • Pain with certain foods or drinks

Many women are told these symptoms are “recurrent UTIs,” even when urine cultures are negative — IC is often the real cause.

Our Comprehensive Evaluation

RoMIUS Urology performs a thorough, gentle evaluation to identify all potential contributors to pelvic or bladder pain:

  • Detailed pelvic examination
  • Pelvic floor muscle assessment
  • Urinalysis & urine culture
  • Cystoscopy when indicated
  • Imaging (ultrasound/CT) if needed
  • Review of hormonal status (perimenopause/menopause)
  • Assessment of bowel function
  • Spine & musculoskeletal screening
  • Sexual health history
  • Diet and triggers review

This multi-angle evaluation allows us to pinpoint the true cause and avoid unnecessary medications or procedures.

Pelvic Floor Muscle Dysfunction

A major cause of pelvic, urethral, and bladder pain is pelvic floor muscle hypertonicity (tightness, spasm, or poor coordination). This can directly mimic:

  • IC symptoms
  • Vaginal burning
  • Painful urination
  • Pain during intercourse
  • Lower abdominal pressure
  • Frequent urination

Treatment includes:

  • Specialized pelvic floor physical therapy
  • Relaxation and breathing techniques
  • Core and posture training
  • Trigger point release
  • Myofascial therapy
  • Coordination training for bladder emptying

We work closely with the region’s top pelvic floor therapists.

IC / Bladder Pain Treatments

For women with true IC, we offer the full spectrum of modern IC therapies:

Lifestyle & Trigger Management

  • Diet modification (IC diet)
  • Hydration strategies
  • Stress reduction

Medical Therapies

  • Oral medications
  • Bladder relaxants
  • Neuromodulators for nerve pain
  • Antihistamines (when mast cell involvement is suspected)

Bladder-Directed Therapies

  • Bladder instillations
  • Heparin/lidocaine rescue instillations
  • Botox® for refractory bladder pain
  • Hydrodistention in select cases

Neuromodulation

  • Sacral neuromodulation (InterStim®) for severe urgency + pain
    (You can choose whether to add your Center of Excellence status here or keep neuromodulation on the OAB page only.)

Addressing Other Causes of Pelvic Pain

Pelvic pain can overlap with or mimic:

  • Urethral stricture or irritation
  • Prolapse
  • Chronic constipation
  • Hormonal genitourinary syndrome (GSM)
  • Vaginal atrophy
  • Endometriosis
  • Nerve entrapment

We coordinate with gynecology, pain specialists, GI, and pelvic floor therapists when interdisciplinary care is beneficial.

Why Women Choose RoMIUS Urology for Pelvic Pain & IC

  • Thorough, gentle evaluation
  • Expertise in IC and bladder-related pain
  • Strong integration with pelvic floor physical therapists
  • Experience treating complex or long-standing symptoms
  • Full spectrum of bladder-directed therapies
  • Focus on root cause—not just symptom suppression
  • Collaborative, holistic care
  • Personalized plans designed for long-term relief
